A Creative Vietnamese Tasting Menu with Highs, Lows, and Thoughtful Flavors
Sep 2026 • Solo
Cơm Cháy — The crispy rice was light and airy, so it wasn’t difficult to bite into. I personally don’t like the gooey texture of eggplant, so this dish wasn’t really for me. It also wasn’t as savory or flavorful as the other two amuse-bouches.

Thịt Mắm Ruốc Betel Leaf — I usually don’t like eating anything with betel leaf because of its herbal character, but I really enjoyed this one. The savory combination of pork, shrimp paste, and pineapple relish was strong enough that the betel leaf didn’t dominate the bite. Everything worked surprisingly well together, making this my favorite of the amuse-bouches.

Chả Giò - This reminded me of a taco. The beef cheek was tender and rich, while the spring-roll wrapper was crispy and delicate. The five-spice definitely elevated the dish and gave the filling more depth and complexity.

Kingfish Chả Cá Lã Vọng — I loved the sauce in this dish since it was elegant and aromatic. The kingfish sashimi tasted fresh and clean, and I appreciated how there was enough acidity and freshness to counter all the oil and richness. Overall, the different elements felt well-balanced.

Pink Pomelo — I liked the interplay of different flavors in this dish, but the tanginess was too pronounced for me, which made the overall composition feel somewhat unbalanced. While I appreciated being able to taste the individual components distinctly, there were some bites where the combination of flavors tasted a little strange to me.

KOTO Fried Chicken — Despite the chicken being tender and juicy, I don’t think there was anything particularly special about this dish. I wish the nước mắm caramel had been more highlighted. Your favorite fast-food chain could probably serve better fried chicken than this.

Slipper Lobster — The lobster was tender and succulent, although I don’t think there was enough lobster meat in the dish. I enjoyed the wok-fired quality, and the aromatics came through nicely. Unfortunately, the overall seasoning was too salty for my taste.

Bánh Hỏi Heo Quay — The pork belly was very well executed: the skin had a satisfying crackle, the fat was soft and properly rendered, and the meat remained tender and juicy. The Cantonese influence was definitely noticeable. However, I wish the sauce had been more emphasized since the flavor of the pork belly dominated the other components. 

The dessert plate was nice. It was my first time trying a pandan waffle, and I really enjoyed the richness and distinctive flavor of the pandan. It was a pleasant way to finish the meal.

The service was excellent. Our server kindly answered all of my questions throughout the meal and was genuinely warm and welcoming.
